reason: The cited evidence (E2) mentions nitriding forming hard nitride phases (AlN, CrN, TiN) and increasing hardness in a different alloy system, but none of the passages provide specific prior evidence for plasma nitriding of TC4, the claimed hardness increase from ~350 to >800 HV, wear reduction, or retention of bulk fatigue/corrosion properties. The premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Plasma nitriding of titanium alloys forms TiN and Ti2N surface layers
Nitride layers increase surface hardness substantially (e.g., from ~350 HV to >800 HV)
Nitride layers reduce wear rates under high-contact stress
The bulk α+β microstructure and its fatigue/corrosion resistance remain largely unaltered after nitriding at ~500°C
